getting_started.label: Getting started
getting_started.title: Ready to use in five steps
getting_started.intro: Follow this order for first-time setup. On the dashboard you can also load a starter template; you see the work-menu choice in the preview and on Starter template created. Change it later via Organisation → Settings → Work menu. One team is enough to start. Time (punch clock) is included; Clock Point remains the sign-in QR.

admin_portal.title: From team to settings
admin_portal.intro: Chapters on the admin portal: team (backoffice, teams and workers), locations, issues, tasks, calendar, reservations, dashboard, Time, unit measurements, optional ESG and IoT Connect, settings, subscription and activity (what happened recently).

internet_portal.title: QR codes on site
internet_portal.intro: Help for unit QR and Clock Point on site: sign-in, reports, unit check, unit measurements, reservations, tasks, photos, work without coverage, new-team-tasks banner and team leader features. The portal screen language is separate from the back office and website: besides Dutch, English, French, German, Spanish and Italian, also Portuguese, Romanian and Polish. More portal languages can be added later. Automatic translation of reports and documents stays with those six languages.

admin_portal.title: Statuses — administrative portal
admin_portal.intro: These statuses are used by administrators to monitor and control the full workflow.
admin_portal.new: The issue has been created; at least one task is waiting for the team to start.
admin_portal.in_progress: Work on the issue is in progress; at least one task is being executed.
admin_portal.done: All tasks for this issue have been completed by the team; the administrator can now approve and close.
admin_portal.closed: The administrator has confirmed completion; the issue is finally closed.

internet_portal.title: Statuses — internet portal
internet_portal.intro: These statuses are aimed at workers in the field and citizens (reporters) to show the direct status of a specific task.
internet_portal.new: The task has been created and is waiting for the team to start.
internet_portal.in_progress: The team is currently on site carrying out the work.
internet_portal.done: The work has been completed by the worker and reported as finished.
internet_portal.closed: The task has been reviewed by the administrator and finally closed.

step_1_text: Start simply: create one team (for example Facility) and add everyone who carries out tasks. Workers sign in with name and icon; a team leader is not required. Link the team to your categories. Larger organisations add extra teams later, or import via CSV/Excel (optionally with location names in the file). Unit-check checklists are under Work → Checklists. Colleague users with login (administrator and employee) are under Team → Backoffice — optionally pick a punch-clock team if they need to clock in themselves. Search large lists via Team → Workers. Link workers and colleagues to locations (empty = everywhere); floater teams may clock in anywhere. Colleagues sign in with email and password, or with Microsoft (the email must match the existing account). Rare actions (team leader, icon, phone, PIN, passkey, deactivate or delete) are in Edit, not on the list. With Time you can set a minimum unpaid break per team on the timesheet (for example 30 minutes).
step_2_text: Group units into categories (for example plumbing, office or electrical). Mark a category as reservable if units should accept time-slot bookings, and turn on Allow reservations per unit (off by default). Optional: require contact details for anonymous QR reporters, and require email confirmation — then the issue is created only after the link in the mail (no account; Clock Point workers exempt). By linking teams to categories, the right team picks up the tasks. Add locations and create units per location — via the form, a bulk series or CSV/Excel. Under Locations → Units you see an organisation-wide overview (filter by location and category, unit count, status and unit-check pills). You can update unit names and descriptions per language. Optional: allow unit measurements and unit checks (category and unit; unit checks off by default) — separate from ESG. Link a checklist per unit (templates under Work → Checklists); the list shows shared checklists and those of teams linked to the category.
step_3_text: First create one or more Clock Points (Team → Teams, or Time → Clock Points if Time is on). Print the QR sticker or print sheet and place it at the entrance, warehouse or workshop — workers sign in here (name + icon). Clocking in/out requires Time. Also print the unit QR from the location or unit detail page and attach it to machines, rooms or assets. Visitors scan the unit QR for issues, documents and optionally reservations. Workers first scan the Clock Point QR, then the unit QR on site for GPS, photos and tasks. On the unit QR they can also run a unit check when category and unit both allow it. Unit measurements (km, temperature, status) via the Measurement tile when set up — no Clock Point required.
step_3_text_time: Create at least one Clock Point (Team → Teams, or Time → Clock Points if Time is on). Print the QR sticker and hang it somewhere visible. Workers scan that QR to sign in (name + icon); clocking in requires Time. Each clock-in, clock-out or move needs scanning again (an open tab is not enough). Also print unit QRs. Then the unit QR on site for GPS, photos and tasks. If the evacuation list is on in Settings (off by default), workers see an Evacuation list tile after sign-in; after confirming that the consultation is exceptional and is logged, they see who is clocked in. Each worker signs in with one phone; a PIN or biometrics (passkey) is optional. Moving between Clock Points too quickly (within 5 minutes) raises an alarm. After sign-in you also see My hours (own shifts for the selected month) and Leave / Absence: request leave, TOIL, sick leave or (if set up) a type under Other; staff decide under Time → Requests. Once WinProx is on the home screen, the worker can turn on push notifications — that button disappears as soon as notifications are allowed. A photo with that request stays with the request for 6 months. After that it stays for one month at the bottom of Subscription.
step_4_text: Issues come in via a QR scan, manual entry or (with IoT Connect) a sensor alarm. If email confirmation is on, the QR issue arrives only after the reporter confirms the link in the mail; in the back office you then see the Reporter confirmed pill. For each issue a task is created automatically and linked to the responsible team. You can create multiple tasks per issue. Set a deadline and track progress via the dashboard, calendar, reservations and Activity.
step_5_text: Workers carry out tasks via the unit QR portal (after signing in via Clock Point); when new team tasks arrive, a banner appears. Once all tasks for an issue have been handled, the administrator can close the issue. Optional: unit checks, unit measurements, ESG, Time presence, IoT Connect and reservations — see the related chapters. Filtered lists support Download report (CSV + print in the same card layout as the back office). Delete organisation data via Subscription (after export in Settings). For inspection rounds, the worker follows stops in a fixed order; on the unit QR they see progress and the next stop. If workers already opened the unit QR online, they can also finish tasks, reports and unit checks without coverage; those sync later. Clock in/out at Clock Point stays online.

hub.technical_sheet_desc: Hosting, GDPR, API, security — for IT (public + printable).
hub.api_webhooks_desc: Integrate with existing software via APIs and webhooks — for decision makers and IT (public + printable).
